==English==
{{wp|<dab>}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|biz||clipping}}
* {{alt|en|bisoness|businesse|busynesse||obsolete}}
* {{alt|en|bizness||pronunciation spelling|{{l|en|AAVE}}}}
* {{alt|en|bidness||Southern pronunciation spelling|{{l|en|AAVE}}}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:bisynes|:afeq|busy|-ness|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|busines}}, {{m|enm|busynes}}, {{m|enm|businesse}}, {{m|enm|bisynes}}, from {{inh|en|ang|bisiġnes|t=business, busyness}}, equivalent to {{suffix|en|busy|ness}}. {{doublet|en|busyness}}. Sense 17 (''something very good, top quality''), possibly derives from "[[the bee's knees]]"

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈbɪz.nɪs/|/ˈbɪz.nɪz/}}<ref>{{R:Jespersen MEGoHP|I|6.63|202|passage=''business'' may sometimes still be heard /bizniz/}}</ref>
* {{IPA|en|/ˈbɪz.nəs/|/ˈbɪz.nəz/|a=weak vowel}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-business.ogg|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-business.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈbɪz.nɪs/|/ˈbɪd.nɪs/|a=Southern American English}}<!-- also /-nəs/ ? -->
* {{hyph|en|busi|ness}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪznɪs|ɪznɪz|ɪznəs|ɪznəz|ɪdnəs|ɪdnəz|s=2}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|countable}} A specific [[commercial]] [[enterprise]] or [[establishment]].
#: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:enterprise}}
#: {{ux|en|I left my father's '''business'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-22|volume=407|issue=8841|page=68
|url=http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21579860-g8-pledges-tackle-three-ts-t-time|title=T time
|passage=The ability to shift profits to low-tax countries by locating intellectual property in them, which is then licensed to related '''businesses''' in high-tax countries, is often assumed to be the preserve of high-tech companies.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130813170650/http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21579860-g8-pledges-tackle-three-ts-t-time}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} A person's [[occupation]], [[work]], or [[trade]].
#: {{ux|en|He is in the motor and insurance '''businesses'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|I'm going to Las Vegas on '''business'''.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} {{U|commercial}}, [[industrial]], or [[professional]] activity.
#: {{ux|en|He's such a poor cook, I can't believe he's still in '''business'''!}}
#: {{ux|en|We do '''business''' all over the world.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} The [[volume]] or [[amount]] of commercial trade.
#: {{ux|en|'''Business''' has been slow lately.}}
#: {{ux|en|They did nearly a million dollars of '''business''' over the long weekend.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|title=No hiding place
|date=2013-05-25|volume=407|issue=8837|page=74
|url=http://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21578357-plan-assess-peoples-personal-characteristics-their-twitter-streams-no
|passage=In America alone, people spent $170 billion on “direct marketing”—junk mail of both the physical and electronic varieties—last year. Yet of those who received unsolicited adverts through the post, only 3% bought anything as a result. If the bumf arrived electronically, the take-up rate was 0.1%. And for online adverts the “conversion” into sales was a minuscule 0.01%. That means about $165 billion was spent not on drumming up '''business''', but on annoying people, creating landfill and cluttering spam filters.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130803110503/http://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21578357-plan-assess-peoples-personal-characteristics-their-twitter-streams-no}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} One's dealings; [[patronage]].
#: {{ux|en|I shall take my '''business''' elsewhere.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} Private [[commercial]] [[interest]]s taken collectively.
#: {{ux|en|This proposal will satisfy both '''business''' and labor.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-08-10|volume=408|issue=8848|author=Schumpeter
|url=http://www.economist.com/news/business/21583242-businesspeople-have-become-too-influential-government-cronies-and-capitols|title=Cronies and capitols
|passage=Policing the relationship between government and '''business''' in a free society is difficult. Businesspeople have every right to lobby governments, and civil servants to take jobs in the private sector.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130816151118/http://www.economist.com/news/business/21583242-businesspeople-have-become-too-influential-government-cronies-and-capitols}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} The management of commercial enterprises, or the study of such management.
#: {{ux|en|I studied '''business''' at Harvard.}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} A particular [[situation]] or [[activity]].
#: {{ux|en|This UFO stuff is a mighty strange '''business'''.}}
#* {{RQ:John Heywood Four PP|sig=[E.ii.]|verso=1|page=81|passage=The wolde ſome mayſter perhappes clowt ye / But as for me ye nede nat doute ye / For I had leuer be without ye / Then haue ſuche '''beſyneſſe''' aboute ye.}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} Any activity or [[objective]] needing to be [[deal with|dealt with]]; especially, one of a [[financial]] or [[legal]] matter.
#: {{ux|en|Our principal '''business''' here is to get drunk.}}
#: {{ux|en|Let's get down to '''business'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Hobbes Leviathan|passage=To know the naturall cause of Sense, is not very necessary to the '''business''' now in hand; and I have els-where written of the same at large.|chapter=Chapter I: Of Sense}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} Something involving one [[personally]].
#: {{syn|en|affair}}
#: {{ux|en|That's none of your '''business'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|My work is no '''business''' of yours.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable|parliamentary procedure}} Matters that come before a body for deliberation or action.
#: {{ux|en|If that concludes the announcements, we'll move on to new '''business'''.}}
# {{lb|en|travel|uncountable}} [[business class|Business class]], the class of seating provided by airlines between [[first class]] and [[coach]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1992|author=James Wallace; Jim Erickson|title=Hard Drive: Bill Gates and the Making of the Microsoft Empire|page=154|url=http://books.google.com/books?id=h1hPAAAAMAAJ
|passage=Gates, who always flew '''business''' or coach, didn't particularly like the high air fares Nishi was charging to Microsoft,{{...}}}}
# {{senseid|en|stage business in theatre}} {{lb|en|acting|theatre}} {{ellipsis of|en|stage business|gloss=aspect of acting}}.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1983|author=Peter Thomson|title=Shakespeare's Theatre|page=155|url=http://books.google.com/books?id=1kQ-AAAAIAAJ|isbn=0710203829
|passage=The '''business''' with the hat is a fine example of the difficulty of distinguishing between 'natural' and 'formal' acting.}}
# {{lb|en|[[Los Angeles]]|informal|with '''''the'''''}} [[Hollywood]], the [[entertainment]] industry.
# {{label|en|slang|with '''''the'''''}} [[prostitution|Prostitution]].
# {{lb|en|countable|collective|rare}} A group of [[ferrets]].
#: {{syn|en|fesnyng}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2004|author=[[w:Dave Duncan (writer)|Dave Duncan]]|title=The Jaguar Knights: A Chronicle of the King's Blades|page=252|url=http://books.google.com/books?id=jEVRHh4y6NUC|isbn=0060555114
|passage=I'm sure his goons will go through the ship like a '''business''' of ferrets, and they'll want to look in our baggage.}}
# {{lb|en|slang|British|with '''''the'''''}} Something very [[good]]; [[top]] [[quality]].
#: {{ux|en|These new phones are the '''business'''!}}
# {{lb|en|slang|uncountable}} The act of [[defecation]], or the [[excrement]] itself, particularly that of a non-human animal.
#: {{ux|en|Your ferret left his '''business''' all over the floor.}}
#: {{ux|en|As the cart went by, its horse lifted its tail and did its '''business'''.}}
# {{lb|en|slang}} {{U|disruptive}} [[shenanigans]]. {{rfex|en}}
# {{lb|en|Australian Aboriginal}} [[matter|Matters]].
#: {{coi|en|[[sorry '''business''']]|a funeral}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj|?}}

# Of, to, [[pertaining]] to{{,}} or used for purposes of [[conduct]]ing [[trade]], [[commerce]], [[governance]], [[advocacy]] or other professional purposes.
#: {{ux|en|Please do not use this phone for personal calls; it is a '''business''' phone.}}
#* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=10|passage=With a little manœuvring they contrived to meet on the doorstep which was {{...}} in a boiling stream of passers-by, hurrying '''business''' people speeding past in a flurry of fumes and dust in the bright haze.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1996|author=Lawyers Co-operative Publishing Company|journal=American Law Reports: Annotations and Cases|volume=35|url=http://books.google.com/books?id=tjI2AQAAIAAJ&q=%22solely+business%22&hl=en&ei=FaaETYaAJsKdccfR-Z4D&sa=X&oi=book_result&ct=result&resnum=20&ved=0CIoBEOgBMBM|page=432|passage={{...}} the fact that the injured party came to the insured premises for solely '''business''' purposes precluded any reliance on the non-business pursuits exception (§ 1 1 2[b]).}}
# [[professional|Professional]], [[businesslike]], having concern for good business practice.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1909|publisher=La Salle Extension University|title=Business Administration: Business Practice|url=http://books.google.com.au/books?id=6lfPAAAAMAAJ&q=%22thoroughly+business+manner%22&dq=%22thoroughly+business+manner%22&hl=en&ei=OHmETb_-O4TCccK9yJcD&sa=X&oi=book_result&ct=result&resnum=1&ved=0CCsQ6AEwAA|page=77|passage={{...}} and the transaction carried through in a thoroughly '''business''' manner.}}
#* {{RQ:Harper's|year=1927|title=Making of America Project|volume=154|url=http://books.google.com/books?id=SRcwAAAAMAAJ&q=%22very+subtle+contrast+becomes%22&hl=en&ei=2cCETaXcBsKPcaH-5YAD&sa=X&oi=book_result&ct=result&resnum=58&ved=0CJYCEOgBMDk4ZA|page=502|passage=Sometimes this very subtle contrast becomes only too visible, as when in wartime Jewish business men were almost lynched because they were thoroughly '''business''' men and worked for profit.}}
# Supporting business, [[conducive]] to the [[conduct]] of business.
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-08|volume=407|issue=8839|page=55
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/business/21579011-president-proposes-new-round-intellectual-property-reform-obama-goes-troll-hunting Obama goes troll-hunting]
|passage=According to this saga of intellectual-property misanthropy, these creatures [patent trolls] roam the '''business''' world, buying up patents and then using them to demand extravagant payouts from companies they accuse of infringing them. Often, their victims pay up rather than face the costs of a legal battle.}}
